chunks: Abu al-Bakhtari Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled concerning a man who died and left heirs, and one of the heirs acknowledged a debt against his father, that this is binding upon him only in his share according to the amount he inherited, and it does not apply to all of his property. فإذا two of the heirs acknowledge it and they are just, that is accepted against the heirs; but if they are not just, they are bound only in their own shares according to what they inherited. Likewise, if some of the heirs acknowledge a brother or a sister, it only binds them in their own share.

And ʿAlī عليه السلام said: Whoever acknowledges a brother, then he is a partner in the property, but his lineage is not established. And if two acknowledge him, then likewise, unless they are just, in which case his lineage is established and he is included with them in the inheritance.

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: the inherited estate or succession property
key_terms.بِدَيْنٍ: a debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.حِصَّتِهِ: his apportioned share of the inheritance
key_terms.عَدْلَيْنِ: two just and trustworthy persons whose acknowledgment is legally accepted
key_terms.نَسَبُهُ: his lineage or legal filial affiliation
key_terms.وَرَثَةً: heirs entitled to inherit from the deceased

ai.seo_question: When does an heir's acknowledgment of a debt or sibling become binding on the rest of the heirs in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings regarding an heir's acknowledgment of a debt owed by the deceased and the acknowledgment of an additional sibling among the heirs. It distinguishes between what is binding only upon the acknowledging heir's share and what can be enforced upon all heirs when the acknowledgment comes from two just witnesses among them.
